findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: Attacker can inject malicious SMTP commands in the email content.
findings.assumptions: The attacker can control the content of the email that is sent through the SMTP server.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.trigger: If the email content is displayed in a web application without proper sanitization, it can lead to XSS.
findings.assumptions: The email content might be displayed in a web application.

findings.title: Improper Input Validation
findings.trigger: The password is read from a file without any validation, which could lead to issues if the file is compromised.
findings.assumptions: The 'secret' file might be accessible or writable by an attacker.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
findings.trigger: The password is read from a file and used directly in the SMTP connection without encryption.
findings.assumptions: The password might be stored in plain text in the 'secret' file.
